analysis.title: US TMT today (SPCX, NFLX)
key_insights: Futures are bid up (NDX +65 bps) alongside global tech strength (KOSPI +3% overnight, Samsung/Hynix +6%). Better SpaceX earnings and commentary may set up a tradeable bounce and give investors confidence that earnings can matter. Focus shifts to META, TTMI, LRCX, TXN in the coming days.

NDX has stabilized this week, but Semis/SOX has barely outperformed despite last week's drawdowns. MU, NVDA, ANET and DELL types are only 1-2% higher on the week. Risk appetite remains limited, and many have lowered conviction on what a durable clearing event could be into year end.
Franchise flows and investor conversations remain back-footed, which suppresses near-term conviction in re-grossing into the same names in short order.

SPCX +8%: investors went in debating where in the previously guided 5-10 GW of capacity by end of 2027 SpaceX could land. Management now cites line of sight to 2.5-3 GW of nameplate compute by year-end and potential to bring an incremental 10 GW online in 2027, with an upside case of more than 20 GW by YE27.

Early investor focus on SPCX: 1) the right framework for Super Intelligence revenues in CY27 (GIR raised 2027 SI revenue by about 70% to about $153bn), 2) pricing visibility and durability of compute returns, 3) execution on Flight 15's goal of capturing booster and ship, 4) Starlink, where management said an investor teach-in on the mobility opportunity could follow.

SpaceX management said new compute at current pricing generates a payback of under 1 year. Earnings call comments imply lower build costs and higher monetization could cut payback to about 6 months in 2027. Management named power, cooling and electrical infrastructure as the primary bottlenecks.
GIR raised CY27 revenue estimates for SpaceX by 50% overnight, after a 55% raise in early August following the C2Q print.

NFLX -7%, about 50% below all-time highs and at new roughly 2-year lows pre-market. Investors debate whether this is a bottom. Questions: whether the ad miss is timing (third-party integration delays) or a growth issue, the fix and timeline for UCAN engagement, normalized growth (low double digits vs high single digits y/y), and the right multiple. The stock trades at 14x GIR's CY28 GAAP EPS estimate of about $4.50.

NFLX positives via GIR: Q3 revenue, operating income and GAAP EPS above prior guidance and GSe/Street, with subscription revenue outperformance and consistent churn despite price increases. Strong 2027 content slate (Narnia, Bridgerton, Wednesday, NFL games, Women's World Cup in the US and Canada). Q3 buybacks of about $4.8bn (vs $4.7bn in Q2) with about $22.3bn left on the authorization.

NFLX negatives via GIR: Q4 revenue, operating income and EPS guide below GSe/Street. FY FCF guide cut from $12.5bn to about $12bn due to a Q4'26 real estate transaction. FY2026 advertising revenue guide of about $2.7bn vs prior about $3bn, on slower ad product rollout from third-party integration delays. Management acknowledged US engagement has room for improvement.
NFLX has de-rated as consensus EPS estimate revisions have stalled.
Today's inbound topics: SPHR +10% yesterday, AI/Semis sentiment, CRM/Braze news, AI supply chain earnings set-ups (TXN, LRCX), SaaS (NOW, WDAY, ADBE up 5-6% this week), and memory sentiment.

Events today: earnings tonight from CCI, IBM, LRCX, META, ROL, TSLA, TXN and United Rentals. NVDA hosts GTC Berlin with a Jensen Huang keynote at 5am ET. Money 20/20 USA, Cloudflare Connect 2026, HR Technology Conference, Global Data Centre & Cloud Expo Canada.

market_movers.rationale: Stock +8% on earnings and capacity commentary. GIR raised CY27 revenue estimates by 50% and CY27 Super Intelligence revenue by about 70% to about $153bn.
Stock -7% to new roughly 2-year lows after weak Q4 guide, an advertising guide cut to about $2.7bn from about $3bn and a lower FCF guide. Trades at 14x GIR's CY28 GAAP EPS estimate of about $4.50.
Stock rose 10% yesterday and was a frequent investor question. The note gives no reason for the move.

sector_views.rationale: Futures bid on global tech strength, but semis have barely outperformed on the week and risk appetite and conviction in re-grossing remain limited.

earnings_insights: SpaceX (SPCX) reported 10/20 evening: stock +8%. Management cited line of sight to 2.5-3GW nameplate compute by YE26 and potential for an incremental 10GW in 2027. Current compute pricing gives under 1-year payback per management, possibly about 6 months in 2027.

Netflix (NFLX) reported Q3: revenue, operating income and GAAP EPS above prior guidance and GSe/Street estimates. Q4 revenue, operating income and EPS guide below prior GSe/Street. FY26 advertising revenue guide about $2.7bn vs prior about $3bn. FY FCF guide about $12bn vs prior $12.5bn. Q3 buybacks about $4.8bn.
Earnings tonight 10/21: CCI, IBM, LRCX, META, ROL, TSLA, TXN, United Rentals. Focus shifts to META, TTMI, LRCX, TXN in the coming days.
risk_factors: SpaceX execution risk: management named power, cooling and electrical infrastructure as the primary bottlenecks.
Industry capacity risk if SPCX executes at the mid to upper end of its GW ambitions.
Durability of SpaceX compute pricing and returns is an open debate.
NFLX: ad rollout delays from third-party integrations, US engagement weakness, estimate revisions stalled, and Q4 guide below Street.
Limited risk appetite and low conviction on a durable clearing event into year end.
vol_and_positioning: Semis/SOX has barely outperformed this week despite last week's drawdowns, with MU, NVDA, ANET and DELL types only 1-2% higher.
Franchise flows and investor conversations remain back-footed, suppressing near-term conviction in re-grossing into the same names.
SaaS names NOW, WDAY and ADBE are up 5-6% this week.
